clue.text: Order one coin restruck

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: a coin restruck is minted afresh, so its letters are recast in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A command to a mint to strike a coin again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restruck' rearranges COIN into ONIC, after I. Order here is a classical style of column, not a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical architectural orders, with scroll-shaped capitals on its columns.

clue.text: Not inclined to be unwell

explanation.surface: Feeling poorly and so reluctant to do anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Indisposed means both unwilling and slightly ill.

clue.text: Imaginary idea a novice concluded

indicators.note: a and novice come at the end, closing the word

parts.note: a notion is an idea
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A beginner's imagined idea brought to its end.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plate a British learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means existing only in theory, hypothetical.

clue.text: It's thrown around but as money is virtually worthless

definitions.text: It's thrown around but as money is virtually worthless

parts.words: It's thrown around but as money is virtually worthless
parts.note: paper scraps tossed at weddings, and a term for currency so devalued it is nearly worthless

explanation.surface: Something flung about freely yet near valueless as cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper bits are thrown over a newly married couple, and hyperinflated banknotes are dismissed as mere paper scraps.

clue.text: What thieves do even before they stop working

explanation.surface: Burglars quitting their trade before they knock off for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even before they' links the two senses: thieves knock off goods, and workers knock off at the end of a shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses this phrase for stealing, and also for finishing one's work for the day.

clue.text: Look up the tower

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to peek is to look quickly

explanation.surface: Gazing upward at a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEEK in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest tower of a castle.

clue.text: No end of treacle spilt on the agreement

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters run out in a new order
no end means the final letter of treacle is lopped off

explanation.surface: Treacle spilled over a signed contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' cuts treacle to TREACL; 'spilt' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a price-fixing agreement between businesses.

clue.text: Go too far with regard to the party

parts.note: over can mean about, concerning
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Overindulging at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo is to take something to excess.

clue.text: Meet with heartless devil

indicators.note: losing the heart means dropping the central letter of the word for devil

parts.note: a fiend is a devil

explanation.surface: Encountering a cruel demon.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to come upon or encounter it.

clue.text: Set off — time to go round school

indicators.note: one piece must go round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a date is a time fixed for something
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: An instruction to set off at a fixed time, circling a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' puts DATE around ETON. Eton College is the well-known English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to explode it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: After exercises, set out embarrassed and harassed

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the first one

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: set out suggests laying the letters out differently, a rearrangement

parts.note: red, as in red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone after a workout feels flushed and hassled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into STE; 'After' places it and RED behind PE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pestered is to be bothered persistently, much like being harassed.

clue.text: See Gavin struggling to contemplate

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters thrash about into a new order

explanation.surface: Watching a man called Gavin struggle to think.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage is to picture or contemplate a possibility.

clue.text: Point to one at bottom farthest behind

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
the one at the bottom is the lowest

explanation.surface: Pointing at the person at the foot of a table.
explanation.definitionFit: The slowest runner trails the field, the one furthest back.

clue.text: It will be an alarming experience to fall over the cable

definitions.text: It will be an alarming experience

parts.note: to trip is to stumble and fall
wire is cable

explanation.surface: Tumbling over a lead is a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: A tripwire sets off an alarm when touched, so it 'alarms' in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping on such a stretched strand triggers an alarm or trap.

clue.text: True lover troubled by boisterous merrymaking

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A sweetheart upset by a noisy party.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel-rout is an old term for a riotous party or rowdy festivity.

clue.text: How the aircrew will escape?

parts.note: fliers fleeing would naturally go by air

explanation.surface: Wondering how pilots get away.
explanation.definitionFit: To take flight means to flee, and literally to fly off.

clue.text: It's a job nobody asked you to do

definitions.text: It's a job nobody asked you to do

parts.words: It's a job nobody asked you to do
parts.note: a chore you set for yourself because no one else imposed it

explanation.surface: A duty that you took on without being asked.
explanation.definitionFit: A task you impose on yourself is one no one else required of you.

clue.text: Syrian capitalists home?

parts.note: read as capital is home: the city that is Syria's seat of government

explanation.surface: Asking where Syrian businessmen live.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient city is the capital of Syria.

clue.text: Coordinating a ruling, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are heard spoken, a homophone

parts.note: ruling lines on paper is lining, so a ruling is a lining

explanation.surface: Coordinating a judge's decision, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruling here is drawn lines, not a verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Aligning things brings them into line, coordinating them.

clue.text: Getting away from French living in tents

parts.note: de is French for from
camping is living under canvas

explanation.surface: Escaping a Frenchman's campsite holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Decamping means leaving hurriedly, slipping off.

clue.text: Mental cases

parts.note: cases holding the mind: skulls enclosing the brain

explanation.surface: A slang phrase for unstable people.
explanation.definitionFit: Skulls are the bony boxes protecting the brain.

clue.text: Might on the border causes confusion

parts.note: may and might are both modal verbs of possibility
a hem is the border of cloth

explanation.surface: Power at the frontier brings chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is chaotic disorder.

clue.text: Len gave translation of the gospel

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, here a reordering of letters

explanation.surface: A man named Len rendered the gospel in another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an older word for the good news of Christ, a gospel.

clue.text: Breaks down any sales arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: An accountant breaks down the figures for a sales deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse something is to break it into parts for study.

clue.text: A particularly incomplete state

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter of the word for particularly is missing

parts.note: very means particularly, as in very much

explanation.surface: An unfinished region of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare firmly.

clue.text: Tax contents of Swiss Cottage

indicators.note: contents means letters held inside the words

explanation.surface: Levy on what's inside a London home.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is a district of north London. Scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: A scot was a medieval levy or payment.

clue.text: Taking hold in an infectious way

explanation.surface: A disease grabbing hold and spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in an ... way' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching means grasping, and a catching illness is one easily passed on.

clue.text: Educate over half who are furthest back

parts.note: to rear a child is to bring up and educate it
most means more than half

explanation.surface: Teaching more than half of those sitting at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmost means at the very rear, last in position.

clue.text: Lot of sense

explanation.surface: Two words: a large amount and a faculty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight more means a lot more, and sight is one of the five senses.
